The builder is most likely to recover **$3,000**, the increase in the homeowner's property value, because a building contractor who is prevented from finishing is generally limited to the benefit the owner actually received. This is a change from my earlier $14,000, which is the pure expectation figure (price minus cost saved, plus the $1,000 resale adjustment) and which the cap rule would override. I'm not certain of that reading, since the expectation measure is the usual starting point and courts vary on whether the benefit cap applies here.

CONFIDENCE: 40
